def current_week_bg(
    week_key: rx.Var[str], fallback: str = "transparent"
) -> rx.Var[str]:
    """Return background color highlighting the current week."""
    return rx.cond(
        week_key == PlanningStore.current_week_key, CURRENT_WEEK_BG, fallback
    )


def week_cell_style(
    week_key: rx.Var[str], fallback: str = "transparent"
) -> dict[str, rx.Var[str]]:
    """Current-week background and month separator for a week column cell."""
    return {
        "backgroundColor": current_week_bg(week_key, fallback),
        "borderLeft": rx.cond(
            PlanningStore.month_start_keys.contains(week_key),
            MONTH_START_BORDER,
            "none",
        ),
    }


def grid_density_vars() -> dict[str, rx.Var[str]]:
    """CSS variables for row height, font size and block gap of the density."""
    compact = PlanningStore.is_compact
    return {
        "--aq-grid-row": rx.cond(compact, "24px", "32px"),
        "--aq-grid-fs": rx.cond(compact, "12px", "0.8125rem"),
        "--aq-grid-gap": rx.cond(compact, "4px", "8px"),
    }

)

def test_month_header_stays_behind_opaque_frozen_column() -> None:
    month = ObjectVar("month", MonthSpan)
def test_employee_header_pins_stats_to_the_right_edge() -> None:
    rendered = str(_employee_header_row(ObjectVar("emp", EmployeeBlock)))
    stats = rendered[rendered.index('["right"] : "0"') :]

    assert '["marginLeft"] : "auto"' in stats
    assert "Geplant" in stats
    assert "Frei" in stats
    assert "Projekt zuweisen" not in stats


def test_empty_grid_row_is_a_small_gap_without_cells() -> None:
    row = empty_grid_row()

    assert row.children == []
    assert BLOCK_GAP == "var(--aq-grid-gap, 8px)"
    assert f'["height"] : "{BLOCK_GAP}"' in str(row)


def test_employee_block_renders_gap_after_gesamt() -> None:
    rendered = str(_employee_block(ObjectVar("emp", EmployeeBlock)))

    assert rendered.index("Gesamt (frei)") < rendered.index(f'"{BLOCK_GAP}"')


def test_project_block_renders_gap_after_gesamt() -> None:
    rendered = str(_project_block(ObjectVar("proj", ProjectBlock)))

    assert rendered.index("Gesamt (allokiert)") < rendered.index(f'"{BLOCK_GAP}"')


def test_team_and_project_gesamt_labels_use_the_same_font_size() -> None:
    employee = ObjectVar("emp", EmployeeBlock)
    project = ObjectVar("proj", ProjectBlock)

    assert 'size:"12px"' in str(_gesamt_row(employee))
    assert 'size:"12px"' in str(_project_gesamt_row(project))


def test_absence_and_internal_values_use_muted_plain_text() -> None:
    cell = ObjectVar("cell", GridCell)

    for render_cell in (_absence_value_cell, _internal_value_cell):
        rendered = str(render_cell(cell))

        assert '["color"] : "var(--alloq-text-muted)"' in rendered
        assert "MantineBadge" not in rendered
        assert "mantine-color-" not in rendered
        assert "borderRadius" not in rendered
        assert 'size:"xs"' in rendered

input.recap: In compact view, project names in the team grid and employee names in the project view now use the grid's 12px font size. Normal view keeps its 14px labels. Tests, lint and typecheck pass, but I haven't checked it in the browser.

content.text:
In compact view, row labels now use the same 12px font size as the grid cells. That covers project names in the team grid and employee names in the project view. Normal view still shows them at 14px. All 423 tests pass, and lint and typecheck are clean. I haven't looked at it in the running app.

The cause was that the label text had a fixed Mantine size (`size="sm"`, 14px), while the grid cells read their size from a CSS variable (`--aq-grid-fs`) that the compact toggle changes.

What changed:
- [planning_shared.py](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/components/planning_shared.py) has a new variable, `--aq-grid-label-fs`, and a constant for it, `ROW_LABEL_FONT_SIZE`. The variable equals the grid font size in compact view and stays at Mantine's `sm` size in normal view.
- The project label in [planning_grid.py:211](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/components/planning_grid.py:211) and the employee label in [planning_project_view.py:137](components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/components/planning_project_view.py:137) now use that constant.
- A new test in [test_planning_grid_rendering.py](components/alloq-project/tests/test_planning_grid_rendering.py) checks that both labels use the new variable.

If you want the labels to match the grid in normal view too (13px instead of 14px), it's a one-line change in the density settings.
